title: Vietnamese Tofu Canh
description: A traditional Vietnamese tofu soup, made with a flavorful broth and topped with fresh herbs. This dish is a staple in Vietnamese cuisine and is often served as a light and comforting meal.

ingredients.name: Tofu
ingredients.notes: Extra-firm tofu works best for this recipe

ingredients.name: Unique mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Use a variety of mushrooms for added depth of flavor

ingredients.name: Umami broth
ingredients.notes: You can also use a combination of chicken and beef broth for added richness

ingredients.name: Canh broth
ingredients.notes: Use a store-bought or homemade canh broth for a rich and savory flavor

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.notes: Use a neutral-tasting oil for frying the tofu

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Use fresh ginger for added depth of flavor

ingredients.name: Chua sauce
ingredients.notes: Use a store-bought or homemade chua sauce for a tangy and sweet flavor

instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the sliced ginger and cook for 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the sliced mushrooms and cook for 2-3 minutes, until they release their liquid and start to brown.
Add the tofu and cook for 2-3 minutes, until it starts to brown.
Pour in the umami broth and canh broth, and bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10-15 minutes, until the flavors have melded together and the tofu is cooked through.
Stir in the chua sauce and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes, until the soup has thickened slightly.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Serve the soup hot, garnished with fresh herbs and a sprinkle of chopped scallions.
